entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Check visa needs on NetherlandsWorldwide. Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

tourism.detail: Australians are generally visa-exempt for short stays in the Netherlands under Schengen rules.
tourism.next: Use NetherlandsWorldwide for the current border and document list.
tourism.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

meetings.detail: Meetings, negotiations, congresses and trade fairs can fit business travel; the official checklist expects an invitation or business evidence.
meetings.next: Carry the invitation, event ticket and business relationship evidence.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.detail: Attending a congress is distinct from being hired to deliver the event programme or provide Dutch services.
conference.next: Confirm attendee versus speaker/trainer status with the organiser.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.route: Host classification; no automatic unpaid-work exemption
unpaid-speaking.detail: A free keynote or panel can still be treated as professional activity depending on duties, reimbursement and organiser. The short-stay checklist is not a work permit.
unpaid-speaking.next: Ask the Dutch host or IND whether the exact unpaid role fits a visitor exception or needs work permission.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.route: Dutch work permit, TWV/single permit or recognised-sponsor route
paid-speaking.detail: Paid speaking, consulting and training for a Dutch organiser are active work; the employer or host normally leads the permission process.
paid-speaking.next: Have the Dutch engager identify the work authorisation and whether a short assignment exemption applies.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Business visit for rights; host-led work or cultural permission for active launch
book-launch.detail: A rights meeting can be business travel, while paid talks, signings, workshops, merchandise or local sales need activity-by-activity treatment.
book-launch.next: Separate publisher meetings from public delivery and retail.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.detail: University teaching and commercial training follow different host and employment classifications.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the university or training client to sponsor the exact teaching arrangement.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.detail: The Netherlands publishes work and residence permits but no simple remote-worker category for an Australian visitor; tax and local-client issues remain separate.
remote-work.next: Confirm residence, payroll and client location before treating a longer stay as remote work.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.route: IND startup or self-employed residence permit
entrepreneur.detail: The startup permit uses a facilitator and viable innovative plan; self-employed residence is assessed against Dutch economic interest and business evidence.
entrepreneur.next: Choose startup versus self-employed and assemble the IND dossier with a Dutch facilitator or adviser.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Short business visit; Dutch operation needs work/business status
trade.detail: Negotiations, sourcing, contracts and fairs can be business travel; fulfilment, installation and local sales may not be.
trade.next: State where goods, services, invoices and delivery occur.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.detail: A performance, exhibition, filming or paid cultural appearance is not automatically covered by visitor entry.
artist.next: Have the promoter confirm performer, crew, fee, venue and labour formalities.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: Schengen visit plus IND/host activation for delivery
mixed-mission.detail: The Netherlands makes the first arrival easy, but the invitation must separate meetings from paid or active work.
mixed-mission.next: Send the whole schedule to the host and ask for one written classification.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, Yarralumla about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, Yarralumla if the host pays you.

volunteering.route: Organisation obtains a UWV volunteer permit
volunteering.detail: Volunteering is work unless the organisation is non-profit and socially beneficial, the work is unpaid and replaces no paid job, and the organisation holds a UWV volunteer permit.
volunteering.next: Ask the organisation to arrange the UWV permit.

laws.rule: The minimum age for buying alcohol and tobacco is 18 years. You can only buy or use marijuana (cannabis) in designated shops if you're a resident of the Netherlands and 18 years or older. You could face criminal penalties, including fines and jail, if: you buy or use cannabis outside of designated places you buy or use cannabis in a designated place, but you're not a resident of the Netherlands you possess or sell illegal drugs or narcotics, including psychoactive 'magic mushrooms'. Taking drugs will weaken your decision-making ability, putting you at greater risk of violence, robbery or sexual assault.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Under Dutch law, everyone over 14 years old must carry an ID. You could show either: a valid passport a driver's licence an identity card or a Dutch residency card Dutch police officers and other authorities can request to see these documents at any time. They may fine you if you can't show your ID.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Doctors are less likely to prescribe antibiotics and other medications compared to what you may be accustomed to. Cold and flu tablets aren't available. For specific information on bringing medication into the Netherlands, read the can I take medication into the Netherlands?
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: For short visits, you'll need both: an International Driving Permit (IDP) a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver’s licences may not be accepted) You must be at least 18 years old to drive. After 185 days, you'll need to apply for a Dutch licence. Car rental companies may require both documents and digital driver's licences may not be accepted. Driving without an IDP where one is required can void your travel and vehicle insurance. You must be at least 21 to hire a car.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency of the Netherlands is the Euro. The Netherlands is a member of the EU. If you travel between the Netherlands and any non-EU country, you must declare over 10,000 euros (or equivalent) cash. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You'll need to pay a fine if you don't declare or give the wrong information on entry or exit. You don't need to declare currency if you're travelling to or from another EU country.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: the Netherlands is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Check visa needs on NetherlandsWorldwide; temporary checks run at the Belgian and German land borders.

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: A Dutch employer, recognised sponsor, university or startup facilitator can supply the documents for the matching permit.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
